piv_multipass — PIV estimate op

• Data kinds: image2d × image2d → flow2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.piv_multipass(a, b, windows=(64, 32), overlap=0.5, peak='gauss3', window_func='hann', outlier_threshold=2.0, normalize='overlap', search_limit=0.25) (to call the implementation directly, import pivops; pivops.piv_multipass(a, b, windows=(64, 32), overlap=0.5, peak='gauss3', window_func='hann', outlier_threshold=2.0, normalize='overlap', search_limit=0.25); from the registry, opspiv.get("piv_multipass"))

• Return value through the ledger: fullseye.ledger.piv_multipass(...) returns only the declared out type flow2d (the underlying function also returns auxiliary values). When you need what was dropped, use fullseye.ledger.piv_multipass.raw(...) or call pivops.piv_multipass directly.

• Underlying return: (flow, info) -> flow2d

Usage

Multi-pass PIV that steps down from coarse windows to fine windows. Returns (flow, info).

The result of each pass is used as the predicted displacement of the next pass (the 2nd image's window is shifted by the integer amount). Removing and filling outliers between passes is intentional —— if a wrong vector is used as-is for the prediction, that window stays wrong, locked in, in the next pass as well.

Args:

a, b: image pair.

windows: sequence of windows in decreasing size. Each pass need not be a multiple of the previous one,

but since the grid changes, the prediction is transferred by nearest neighbour.

overlap / peak / window_func: same as piv_cross_correlate.

outlier_threshold: threshold of the normalised median test between passes. None disables it.

Returns:

(flow, info) of the final pass. info["passes"] holds the window size of each pass.
